title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the framework behind its production service
friendlyTitle: DeepSeek publishes the software it uses to run its own models
summary: DeepSeek has published DeepInfer, the inference framework it says powers its large-scale production services. The Apache-2.0 release supports offline inference for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, including the 17 October checkpoint, with optimized kernels, expert parallelism, and structured outputs. DeepSeek says the project was originally built primarily on vLLM. The repository reached about 11,300 stars within a day of the first commit, and the Hacker News thread passed 1,900 points.
friendlySummary: DeepSeek has published DeepInfer, the software it says it uses to run its models for customers at large scale. The licence is Apache 2.0. The first supported model is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, including the 17 October version. DeepSeek says the project started from vLLM, another open serving tool. The repository reached about 11,300 stars in a day, and the Hacker News discussion passed 1,900 points.
whyItMatters: If you already run DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, this is the serving code the lab says it uses, not a new model and not a hosted API. It is a large-GPU stack, not a laptop download. The open release does not change the separate US order, published the same day, that tells civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products from their systems.
